_id: best007 with the ground oscillator changed to the Microchip 5071B caesium beam, Monte Carlo on at 12 seeds x 3600 s. The twin of best002cs, on the rung that carries the integer-ambiguity claim.
_delta: clock.customOscillators.CS5071B declared and clock.tower.clockType RUBIDIUM -> CS5071B, exactly as best002cs applies it. The raw-carrier-row construction, band, product interval and Monte-Carlo block are inherited unchanged. Read this rung against best007mc, which differs from it by the ground oscillator alone.
_WHATTHEGROUNDOSCILLATORCANANDCANNOTREAC: The ambiguity result this rung carries -- undifferenced float sigma 0.0080 m = 0.066 cycles, inside the 0.15-cycle gate -- came from removing the ionosphere-free carrier row, which is a row-construction change and has nothing to do with the tower oscillator. So the ambiguity number should be essentially UNCHANGED and that is the expected outcome, not a disappointment. What the oscillator can reach is the tower clock residual entering every code and carrier row from that tower, so if anything moves it is the clock channel and, through it, the converged position.
_THEONECOUPLINGWORTHWATCHING: There IS a path from the ground clock to the ambiguity, and it is the reason this rung is worth running rather than assumed. The undifferenced carrier ambiguity absorbs anything constant per (tower, antenna) and anything the filter cannot separate from the receiver clock. A tower clock residual that is smoother has a different spectral overlap with the ambiguity state than one that is noisier, so the ambiguity SIGMA can move even when the position does not. If the ambiguity sigma degrades past 0.15 cycles under a better oscillator, that would be a real and counterintuitive finding about which state absorbs what, and it is cheap to check on a rung already being run.
_READTHEVERDICTFIRST: As on best007mc, an OPTIMISTIC Monte-Carlo verdict withdraws the ambiguity claim without touching the position result, because position is truth-referenced and the ambiguity gate is a covariance statement. carr018 is the standing worked example: bootstrap P(success) 0.999999 with 9 of 20 integers wrong.

clock._source: Microchip 5071B, caesium beam. Same h-coefficients as best002cs; the two rungs must declare them identically or the pair stops being a controlled comparison.
clock._h2AndH1AreZeroed: h2 (white PM) is set to 0 rather than the source table's 8.0e-30, and h1 was already 'n.s.'. This is FORCED and it is free. TowerClockCorrectionProvider.frequencyWanderVar_ REFUSES to run on a nonzero h2/h1 (error id h2h1Uncharged): ClockModel.precomputeNoise folds h2/h1 into the synthesised truth frequency series, but frequencyWanderVar_ has no rate-domain charge for them, so R would be knowingly optimistic. Overriding that via cfg.validation.unsupportedFeaturePolicy = 'disableWithWarning' was rejected: this rung exists to Monte-Carlo the covariance, so deliberately seeding a known R defect into it would answer nothing. COST OF ZEROING IT, computed against the same three-term model the code implements plus the standard white-PM term 3*f_h*h2/(4 pi^2 tau^2) at the 1 s grid's Nyquist f_h = 0.5 Hz: h2 is 2.0e-10 of the total Allan variance at tau = 20 s and 8.1e-10 at tau = 5 s, so sigma_y is IDENTICAL TO SEVEN SIGNIFICANT FIGURES either way (1.936549e-12 at 20 s in both cases). Every built-in class in oscillatorCatalog_ carries h2 = h1 = 0 for the same reason, so this part is entered on exactly the footing the shipped catalogue uses.
